question.problem: The lateral surface area of a cylinder is $864\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{2}$ and the ratio of its height to its radius is $3.$ Calculate the radius of the cylinder.

current_example.problem: The lateral surface area of a cylinder is $900\pi \: \textrm{in}^2$ and the ratio of its height to its radius is $2.$ Calculate the radius of the cylinder.
current_example.worked_solution:
Let $r$ and $h$ be the radius and height of the cylinder, respectively. 

We are given that 

$$
\dfrac{h}{r}=2
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
h=2r.
$$

We can find the lateral surface area of a cylinder using the formula

$$
S_L =  2\pi rh.
$$

Substituting the values

$$
S_L=900\pi, \qquad h=2r
$$

into the formula for $S_L,$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{L} & =2\pi rh \\ 900\pi  & =2\pi r(2r) \\ 900\pi  & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{900\pi }{4\pi } \\ {r}^{2} & =225 \\ r & =15\,\text{in}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we disregard the negative solution since length must be positive.
